newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline differentials ease.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline differentials ease.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials eased on Friday, offsetting gains in NYMEX front-month unleaded futures prices, traders said.
"I think it's a reality check," one trader said of the moderating gasoline differentials, which had remained steady as NYMEX futures prices rallied through the week.

Diesel fuel differentials were largely unchanged as trade wound down for the week in the Chicago and Group Three cash markets, but some bullish sentiment was brewing in those barrels as well, traders said.
Distillate basis was expected to move lower next week in the Midwest after a flood of product was shipped into the market and refineries reported a 1.13 million barrel build in inventories on hand.
"There's a 36-day supply of low sulphur diesel in the Williams (pipeline) system," one trader said. "That's the highest level since last February."

The Williams system, a key barometer of inventories in the Midwest, reported a 21-day supply of gasoline on hand following API's report of a 2.98 million barrel draw in gasoline stocks at the region's refineries.
Chicago prompt unleaded was bid 0.75 cent under the print, with later deliveries bid 1.0 cent under the print.
Group Three prompt unleaded was talked 0.75/1.0 cent over the print, with later deliveries 1.0/0.75 cent under.
High sulphur diesel was talked 0.25 cent over the print in Chicago and 2.0 cents over in Group Three, traders said.
